target_customer: Patients at risk of sepsis outside hospitals and the health systems or clinicians monitoring them
problem: Sepsis is deadly and fast, and early signs are missed outside the hospital. The company aimed to use a wearable and AI to flag deterioration early.
business_model: Wearable device plus AI early-warning software, sold to health systems; grant funded in later years
product_category: Wearable medical device and sepsis prediction AI

founders.name: Robert Quinn
founders.background_notes: The YC page gives no bio.

founders.name: Wei-Jien Tan
founders.background_notes: YC page says background in electrical engineering and physiology, a neuroscience lab applying machine learning to brain recordings, then implantable medical device firmware and electronics, where he met his cofounder. No schools or employers named.

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining a body-worn sensor with clinically validated sepsis prediction needs hardware, signal processing, machine learning and regulatory validation from a team of five.

defensibility.rationale: Clinical validation and device clearance would be hard to copy, but no evidence of cleared product or proprietary data was found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move was found. The company was eventually acquired by Cytovale, a sepsis diagnostics firm.

market_need_then: Sepsis is a leading cause of hospital death and a known target for early detection, but no dated source on demand for out-of-hospital wearable monitoring was found.

branding.domain_note: No company website is listed in the directory data.

rebrands.why: No reason found; the new name states the product focus

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand was found and the company stayed tiny.

pivots.to: Sepsis Scout, wearables and AI for sepsis prediction
pivots.why: Not stated in any source; the rename and sepsis focus are shown on the YC page

outcome_analysis: Sepsis Scout stayed a very small team, with only an accelerator-scale funding trace and a federal NIH grant of about 254 thousand dollars for 2022 to 2024. It was eventually absorbed by Cytovale, which raised an 84 million dollar Series C in 2023. The terms and the reasons are not public, so the exit may be a soft landing, but that is not confirmed.
